record_type_quote:
Our  pri-
mary  aim  was  to  extend  this  result.  We  used  an  improved 
design  which  allows  us  to  replicate  the  previous  effect 
obtained by Guo et al. (2022b), but to further disentangle the 
effect of infection status on various components of long-term 
memory, namely, memory type (item versus associative) and 
stimulus  type  (verbal  versus  non-verbal).  To  this  end  we 
analysed data from a modified version of the Guo et al. (2022b)
study, which includes verbal and nonverbal versions of both 
item  and  associative  memory  task,  collected  online  from 
a new cohort of participants.

The general overall wording is the reason for selecting successful rather than inferring a mixed overall verdict.
